White plays Kxg5 to capture the pawn. But that doesn't matter—Black is clearly better with rook vs bishop+pawn when Black still has an advanced pawn on h4.

This is the winning line! The move is **h4+** and it leads to winning White's rook.

**Best move:** h4+

**Main line:** h4+ Kg4 Rb4+ f4 Rg7+ Kxg7

**Motif:** Attraction (forcing the king forward with the pawn check), then deflection (driving the rook away with a check)

**Explanation:**
h4+ forces White's king to g4 (the only legal move), bringing it dangerously forward. Black then plays Rb4+ which forces f4 (blocking the check), and after Rg7+ White's rook is pinned and attacked—Kxg7 wins it cleanly. You win White's rook by using tempo and the king's poor placement to exploit its loose position. Always look for forcing moves (checks) that improve your position with tempo.
